scenes.title: Do these 3 points lie on ONE line?
body: Collinear = all points lie on the same straight line
scenes.narration: Here’s the problem: do the points A one comma three, B three comma seven, and C five comma eleven all lie on one straight line? The idea is not just to calculate two slopes. Collinear means the direction from one point to the next never changes. Slope is how we measure that direction.

scenes.title: Why slope is the test
scenes.narration: Slope compares vertical change with horizontal change. If A to B and B to C have the same ratio, both segments point in exactly the same direction, so they form one straight line. This is where students often mix things up: matching just the y changes or just the x changes is not enough. The ratio must match.

scenes.title: First segment: A to B
scenes.narration: From A to B, y rises by four while x increases by two. So the slope is four divided by two, which is two. Notice why subtraction order matters: if you reverse the points in the numerator, you must also reverse them in the denominator. Reversing only one creates the wrong sign.

scenes.title: Second segment: B to C
scenes.narration: Now from B to C, the rise is again four and the run is again two, so the slope is two. The two slopes match. That means the direction did not bend at B. The three points stay on one straight line.

scenes.title: Quick check and recap
scenes.narration: Quick check: all three points satisfy y equals two x plus one, confirming they lie on the same line. So remember the idea: collinear points keep one constant direction, and for a nonvertical line, equal pairwise slopes prove that. For a vertical line, slope is undefined, so instead check that every x coordinate is the same. The full lesson is available on SUMMIT. Find the complete lesson below.
